newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson-CSF staff seek sell-off decision.
newsitem.headline: Thomson-CSF staff seek sell-off decision.

text.p: The employee shareholder association of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF called on Tuesday for the resumption of its privatisation, launched under the previous conservative government.

The APAT (Association du Personnel Actionnaire de Thomson) said in a statement it "hopes that a procedure for the gradual divestment by the state will be put in place, which is a necessary condition for European development".
The Socialists indicated during their campaign that they would stop all privatisations, particularly the Thomson-CSF sale, in which Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom are rivals.
Analysts have said the sell-off of the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF could raise around 10 billion francs.
"We favour a divestment by the government and a disengagement by the state below 50 percent," APAT Chairman Michel Hanotte told Reuters.

The APAT "noted" the change in the majority and asked the Socialist government of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, which is due to be formed on Wednesday or Thursday, "that an analysis of the means and strengths available should be done immediately, so as to determine the future direction for Thomson-CSF."
"Eight heavy months of uncertainty" have weighed on Thomson-CSF which have paralysed the group while the American and European business electronics industries have been reorganising, it said.
The Socialists have talked about creating a large aerospace group bringing in combat plane maker Dassault Aviation, civilian aircraft and missiles group Aerospatiale and Thomson-CSF.
APAT was set up in 1995 when President Jacques Chirac launched the privatisation drive and numbers some 3,000 members.
